title_en: Agricultural Bank of China, Changsha Xianfeng Branch v. Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd. and Changsha Jinxia Development & Construction Co., Ltd. — dispute over a loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: The reasons for discrepancies in the content of contract texts held by the parties to a contract are complex and varied, and it cannot simply be concluded on this basis that one party has engaged in intentional fraud. If one party to the contract claims that the other party has committed malicious fraud based on such discrepancies, it must provide other evidence to prove the claim.

full_text_en:
Agricultural Bank of China, Changsha Xianfeng Sub-branch v.

Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd. and Changsha Jinxia

Development & Construction Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan guaranty contract

【Ruling Summary】

The reasons for discrepancies in the content of contract texts held separately by the parties to a contract are complex and varied, and one cannot simply conclude that a particular party to the contract engaged in intentional fraud based on such discrepancies alone. If a party to the contract claims that the other party committed malicious fraud on this basis, it must provide additional evidence to prove such claim.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 33

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Changsha Jinxia Development & Construction Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Inside the Government of Laodaohe Township, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Cao Hongjie, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Pan Bingwu, Attorney at Law, Boao Law Firm, Hunan.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ziren, Attorney at Law, Boao Law Firm, Hunan.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Agricultural Bank of China, Changsha Xianfeng Sub-branch, domiciled at: No. 538, Section 1, Furong Middle Road, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Responsible Person: Tang Chuntao, Branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Tingkai, Attorney at Law, Fugong Law Firm, Beijing.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at: 12th Floor, Jinfan Building, No. 524, Section 1, Furong Middle Road, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Xiang Jun, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Cao Zhiwei, Director of Risk Control Department of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Huisheng, Legal Advisor of the Company.

Appellant Changsha Jinxia Development & Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinxia Company), in the case of dispute over loan guaranty contract with Appellee Agricultural Bank of China, Changsha Xianfeng Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch) and Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinfan Company), being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2006) Xiang Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 30 rendered by the Hunan High People's Court, appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of presiding judge Qian Xiaochen, and acting judges Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu, to hear this case, with court clerk Yuan Hongxia recording. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on September 26, 2006, requesting judgment: 1. Order Jinfan Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 39.95 million and interest accrued up to September 20, 2006, in the amount of RMB 6,471,372.74, with corresponding interest from September 20, 2006, until the date of actual enforcement calculated at the overdue loan interest rate; 2. Order that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch has the right to be paid in priority from the mortgaged property of Jinxia Company; 3. Order Jinfan Company and Jinxia Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance found after trial: (1) On December 12, 2001, Jinfan Company submitted a "Application for Working Capital (Short-term) Loan" to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, applying for a loan of RMB 40 million, with the purpose of the loan being "repaying old loans with new borrowings." Jinxia Company affixed its official seal as a guarantor on the said "Application," and noted "agree to provide mortgage guarantee with the land of the cooperative parties, no other forms of guarantee."

On December 29, 2001, Jinfan Company (borrower) and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch (lender) entered into the "Loan Contract" numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Jie Zi (2001) No. 041, stipulating: the loan amount is RMB 40 million, the loan type is "short-term loan," the loan purpose is "repaying old loans with new borrowings," and the loan disbursement and repayment dates are December 31, 2001, and December 31, 2002, respectively. On the 31st of the same month, the parties executed the "Loan Certificate" for the said RMB 40 million.

On December 29, 2001, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch (mortgagee), Jinfan Company (debtor), and Jinxia Company (mortgagor) entered into the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Gao Di Zi (2001) No. 0024, stipulating: the mortgagor voluntarily provides guarantee for all types of business handled by the debtor with the mortgagee from December 30, 2001, to December 31, 2003, with a maximum outstanding balance of RMB 52.38 million; the mortgagor agrees to use the planned plots No. 5 and No. 7 in Jinxia New District as collateral. Subsequently, Jinxia Company registered the planned plots No. 5 and No. 7 in Jinxia New District and obtained the "Certificate of Land Rights and Interests" Chang Guo Tu Ta Xiang (2002) Zi No. 066, with the mortgagee being ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, and the term of the rights set from December 30, 2001, to December 31, 2003.

(2) On November 30, 2002, Jinxia Company issued a "Letter of Commitment to Provide Mortgage Guarantee for Loans of Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd. from the Bank" to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, stating: "On December 30, 2001, our company provided mortgage guarantee for the loan of RMB 52.38 million obtained by Hunan Jinfan Economic Development Company from ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch using the land parcels Jinxia New District No. 5 (area 48,563.34 square meters, land appraised value RMB 34,892,760) and No. 7 (area 55,585.48 square meters, land appraised value RMB 39,938,167). Now, due to the separation and restructuring of Hunan Jinfan Economic Development Company into Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd., our company agrees to provide mortgage guarantee for the RMB 52.38 million short-term working capital loan of Hunan Jinfan Investment Management Co., Ltd. from ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch using the land parcels Jinxia New District No. 5 and No. 7, and to fulfill the corresponding mortgage guarantee obligations."

On December 31, 2002, Jinfan Company (borrower) and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch (lender) entered into the "Loan Contract" numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Jie Zi (2002) No. 0047, stipulating: the loan amount is RMB 40 million, the loan type is "working capital," the loan purpose is "repaying old loans with new borrowings," and the loan disbursement and repayment dates are December 31, 2002, and December 31, 2003, respectively. On the same day, the parties executed the "Loan Certificate" for the said RMB 40 million.

(3) On December 31, 2003, Jinfan Company (borrower) and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch (lender) entered into the "Loan Contract" numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Jie Zi (2003) No. 0062, stipulating: the loan amount is RMB 39.95 million, the loan type is "working capital loan"; the loan disbursement and repayment dates are December 31, 2003, and December 31, 2004, respectively; the annual interest rate for the loan under this contract is 6.903%, with monthly interest settlement on the 20th day of each month; if the borrower fails to repay the loan principal within the agreed term, the lender has the right to charge overdue interest on the overdue amount at a daily rate of 0.21 per thousand for the number of days overdue; for interest payable but not paid, the lender has the right to charge compound interest at the prevailing interest rate; the guarantee method for the loan under this contract is mortgage, and a separate guarantee contract shall be executed; this contract is made in triplicate, one copy for each party and the guarantor. On the same day, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company executed the "Loan Certificate" for the said RMB 40 million.

Regarding the agreement on "loan purpose," the "Loan Contract" held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch (lender) and that held by Jinxia Company (guarantor) are inconsistent: the "Loan Contract" (original) provided by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch stipulates the loan purpose as "working capital loan for repaying old loans with new borrowings" (handwritten); whereas the "Loan Contract" (original) provided by Jinxia Company stipulates the loan purpose only as "working capital" (handwritten), without the phrase "loan for repaying old loans with new borrowings."

Furthermore, the "Loan Contract" held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and that held by Jinxia Company also differ in three other aspects: 1. In the "Other Matters" column of Article 8 of the contract, the contract held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch contains a handwritten note: "This contract is secured by mortgage contracts numbered 430108001 Nong Yin Di Zi 2003 No. 0053 and 430108001 Nong Yin Di Zi 2003 No. 0054," while this column is blank in the contract held by Jinxia Company; 2. On the contract held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, Xiang Jun, the legal representative of Jinfan Company, affixed his personal seal, whereas on the contract held by Jinxia Company, Xiang Jun's signature appears; 3. On the contract held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch affixed its "Loan Contract Special Seal," whereas on the contract held by Jinxia Company, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch affixed its administrative official seal.

(4) On December 31, 2003, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch (mortgagee) and Jinxia Company (mortgagor) entered into two "Mortgage Contracts" numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Di Zi (2003) No. 0053 and (430108001) Nong Yin Di Zi (2003) No. 0054, respectively, stipulating: to ensure the due performance of the "Loan Contract" (master contract) numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Jie Zi (2003) No. 0062 entered into between Jinfan Company (debtor) and the mortgagee, and to protect the realization of the mortgagee's claims, the mortgagor is willing to provide mortgage guarantee for the debts formed by the debtor with the mortgagee under the master contract; the mortgagor uses the planned plots No. 7 (valued at RMB 39,938,167) and No. 5 (valued at RMB 34,892,760) in Jinxia New District as collateral to secure working capital loans of RMB 20 million and RMB 19.95 million, respectively; the scope of the mortgagor's guarantee includes the principal, interest, overdue interest, compound interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, compensation for losses, and all expenses incurred by the mortgagee for realizing the claims, such as litigation fees, attorney fees, collateral disposal fees, and transfer fees. Subsequently, Jinxia Company registered the planned plots No. 7 and No. 5 in Jinxia New District and obtained the "Certificates of Land Rights and Interests" Chang Guo Tu Ta Xiang (2002) Zi No. Xu 066-1 and Chang Guo Tu Ta Xiang (2002) Zi No. Xu 066-2, respectively, with the mortgagee being ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch. The two "Certificates of Land Rights and Interests" state: the plot numbers for the planned plots No. 7 and No. 5 in Kaifu District, Changsha, Jinxia New District, are both 5999997, the nature of ownership is "state-owned," the type of use rights is "granted," the land area of plot No. 7 is 55,585.48 square meters, and the land area of plot No. 5 is 48,563.34 square meters.

(5) On December 1, 2004, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch issued a "Notice of Loan Maturity" to Jinfan Company, stating that the loan principal of RMB 39.95 million and corresponding interest under the "Loan Contract" numbered (430108001) Nong Yin Jie Zi (2003) No. 0062 would mature on December 31, 2004, and requiring Jinfan Company to prepare funds for repayment when due. Jinfan Company acknowledged receipt by affixing its seal on the notice. On January 4, 2005, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch issued a "Notice of Debt Overdue Collection" to Jinfan Company, demanding payment of the overdue principal of RMB 39.95 million and corresponding interest, and Jinfan Company acknowledged receipt by affixing its seal on the notice.

On December 31, 2004, Jinxia Company issued a letter to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, stating: "Changsha Jinxia Development & Construction Corporation signed the 'Mortgage Contracts' with your bank on December 31, 2003, numbered Nong Yin Di Zi (2003) No. 0053 and No. 0054, respectively. The purpose of the principal debt secured by the above mortgages was working capital loans. The restructuring of Changsha Jinxia Development & Construction Corporation into Changsha Jinxia Development & Construction Co., Ltd. in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China is now substantially completed. Our company has learned that the loan purpose of the principal debtor, Jinfan Company, is the refinancing of old loans with new borrowings from your bank. Our company objects to the loan purpose of the principal debtor and refuses to allow your bank to exercise the mortgage rights over our company's assets." On the same day, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch issued a "Reply Letter" to Jinxia Company, stating: "The mortgage guarantee provided by your company on December 31, 2003, under the 'Mortgage Contracts' numbered Nong Yin Di Zi (2003) No. 0053 and No. 0054 for the loan of RMB 39.95 million to Jinfan Company is lawful and valid, and there are no legal doubts. Please strictly fulfill your obligations as guarantor." On January 4, 2005, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch issued a "Notice for Guarantor to Fulfill Liability" to Jinxia Company, requiring Jinxia Company to immediately fulfill its guarantee obligations for the overdue principal of RMB 39.95 million and corresponding interest. The above "Reply Letter" and "Notice for Guarantor to Fulfill Liability" were served on Jinxia Company by the Changsha Notary Public Office on January 14, 2005, and the Changsha Notary Public Office issued a "Notarial Certificate" (2005) Chang Zheng Nei Zi No. 182 in respect thereof.

(6) After the said loan of RMB 39.95 million matured on December 31, 2004, Jinfan Company has not repaid the loan principal to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, and has accrued overdue interest since September 21, 2004. During this litigation, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, based on the normal annual interest rate of 6.903% and the overdue annual interest rate of 7.56%, calculated that the total overdue interest owed by Jinfan Company as of November 20, 2006, amounts to RMB 7,067,934.41.

The court of first instance held after trial: In this case, the three "Loan Contracts" entered into between Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch on December 29, 2001, December 31, 2002, and December 31, 2003, respectively, are all legally valid. Considering the intrinsic relationship among the three loan contracts and the actual use of the loans, the loan under each subsequent loan contract was used to "repay old loans with new borrowings" under the preceding loan contract. Therefore, only the "Loan Contract" dated December 31, 2003, should be taken as the basis for determining the rights and obligations between ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company, and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch is also asserting its rights against Jinfan Company based on the loan of RMB 39.95 million under this loan contract. Jinfan Company's failure to repay the loan principal of RMB 39.95 million and the corresponding interest on time is the direct cause of this dispute, and it shall bear the civil liability to repay the loan principal of RMB 39.95 million and the corresponding interest to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch in accordance with the law.

The "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" entered into among ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, Jinfan Company, and Jinxia Company on December 29, 2001, and the two "Mortgage Contracts" entered into between ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinxia Company on December 31, 2003, were all mortgage guarantees provided by Jinxia Company using the land use rights of the planned plots No. 5 and No. 7 in Kaifu District, Changsha, Jinxia New District, which it had the right to dispose of, for the loans of Jinfan Company from ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch. These represented the true intentions of the parties involved, and the mortgage registration procedures for the land use rights were conducted in accordance with the law; therefore, the above mortgage contracts should all be deemed legally valid. Since Jinxia Company, in its capacity as guarantor, affixed its official seal to the "Application for Working Capital (Short-term) Loan" issued by Jinfan Company to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch on December 12, 2001, which clearly stated the purpose of the RMB 40 million loan application as "repaying old loans with new borrowings," Jinxia Company, when providing the maximum amount mortgage guarantee on December 29, 2001, was aware that the purpose of the RMB 40 million loan stipulated in the "Loan Contract" entered into on the same day between Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch was "repaying old loans with new borrowings." According to Article 39, Paragraph 1, of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (Shen Fa Shi [2000] No. 44), which states: "Where the parties to the principal contract agree to repay an old loan with a new loan, the surety shall not bear civil liability unless the surety knew or should have known," a surety who, knowing or being deemed to know that the parties to the principal contract have agreed to "repay old loans with new borrowings," still provides a guarantee, shall bear the guarantee liability. By reference to this interpretation, in this case, Jinxia Company, knowing that Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch had agreed that the purpose of the RMB 40 million loan was "repaying old loans with new borrowings," nevertheless provided a maximum amount mortgage guarantee of RMB 52.38 million for the RMB 40 million "refinancing" loan under the "Loan Contract" signed between Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch on December 29, 2001. Therefore, Jinxia Company shall bear the mortgage guarantee liability for this loan in accordance with the law.

Given that the Maximum Mortgage Contract dated December 29, 2001 was a guarantee for the Loan Contract dated December 29, 2001 and the Loan Contract dated December 31, 2002, and the two Mortgage Contracts dated December 31, 2003 were guarantees for the Loan Contract dated December 31, 2003, and since the Loan Contract dated December 31, 2003 was objectively a "new loan to repay the old loan" for the loans under the two Loan Contracts dated December 29, 2001 and December 31, 2002, in this case, Jinxia Company should only assume mortgage guarantee liability for the loan under the Loan Contract of the same date based on the two Mortgage Contracts dated December 31, 2003. Although the Loan Contract dated December 31, 2003 held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch stipulates the loan purpose as "working capital loan for new loan to repay old loan," the Loan Contract held by Jinxia Company stipulates the loan purpose as "working capital," not "new loan to repay old loan." Furthermore, on December 31, 2004, Jinxia Company issued a letter to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch expressing objection to the purpose of Jinfan Company's loan as "new loan to repay old loan." Therefore, it should be determined that when Jinxia Company provided the mortgage guarantee on December 31, 2003, it did not know and should not have known that the actual purpose of the RMB 39.95 million loan under the Loan Contract of the same date was "new loan to repay old loan." According to Article 39, Paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Where the parties to the principal contract agree to use a new loan to repay an old loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known of such agreement," and Paragraph 2, which provides: "Where the new loan and the old loan are guaranteed by the same guarantor, the preceding paragraph shall not apply," if the new loan and the old loan are guaranteed by the same guarantor, the guarantor shall still bear liability even if the guarantor did not know or should not have known of the agreement between the parties to the principal contract for a "new loan to repay the old loan." By the same reasoning, where the parties to the principal contract agree to a "new loan to repay the old loan," and the new loan and the old loan are secured by the same mortgagor, the mortgagor cannot be exempted from mortgage guarantee liability. Therefore, even though Jinxia Company did not know or should not have known at the time it provided the mortgage guarantee on December 31, 2003 that the RMB 39.95 million loan being guaranteed was for a "new loan to repay the old loan," since the new loan of RMB 39.95 million and the old loan of RMB 40 million under the Loan Contract dated December 29, 2001 and the Loan Contract dated December 31, 2002 were both guaranteed by the same mortgagor, Jinxia Company, with the same collateral, and since Jinxia Company's guarantee for the new loan of RMB 39.95 million did not increase its guarantee liability for the old loan of RMB 40 million, Jinxia Company should still bear mortgage guarantee liability for the RMB 39.95 million loan principal owed by Jinfan Company under the Loan Contract dated December 31, 2003 and the corresponding interest, within the scope of guarantee stipulated in the two Mortgage Contracts dated December 31, 2003. Jinxia Company's defense that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch did not actually disburse the RMB 39.95 million working capital loan to Jinfan Company and that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch does not have a mortgage right against Jinxia Company is untenable, and this Court does not accept it.

The Loan Contract signed between Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch on December 31, 2003 expressly stipulates: the annual interest rate for the loan under this contract is 6.903%, with interest settled monthly; if the borrower fails to repay the loan principal within the agreed term, the lender has the right to charge overdue interest on the overdue loan at a daily rate of 0.21 per thousand based on the number of overdue days; for accrued but unpaid interest, the lender has the right to charge compound interest at the applicable interest rate. This content represents the true intention of both parties, does not violate mandatory provisions of national laws or administrative regulations, and should be valid. Furthermore, the stipulation in the Loan Contract regarding charging overdue interest at a daily rate of 0.21 per thousand is consistent with the banking system's calculation of overdue interest at an annual rate of 7.56% (0.21%o per day x 360 days = 7.56%). Therefore, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch's calculation in this case, based on the Loan Contract's stipulations regarding normal interest rate, overdue interest rate, and compound interest, using the normal annual rate of 6.903% and the overdue annual rate of 7.56%, resulting in a total overdue interest owed by Jinfan Company as of November 20, 2006 of RMB 7,067,934.41, is correct, and this Court accepts it. Jinfan Company's argument that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch's calculation of interest does not conform to the Loan Contract's stipulations, and Jinxia Company's opinion that the interest in this case should not be calculated according to the Loan Contract's stipulations, are not accepted by this Court.

In conclusion, Jinfan Company should repay ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch the outstanding loan principal of RMB 39.95 million and the corresponding interest. If Jinfan Company fails to perform this debt, Jinxia Company shall bear mortgage guarantee liability using the land use rights of the planned plots No. 5 and No. 7 in Jinxia New District, Kaifu District, Changsha City, which it provided as collateral. Therefore, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch's claims for Jinfan Company to repay the outstanding loan principal and interest and for priority repayment from the proceeds of the sale of Jinxia Company's mortgaged property are established, and this Court supports them. Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 196, 198, 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 33, 34(1)(iii), 38, 41, 46, and 57 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and with reference to Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment: 1. Jinfan Company shall repay ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch the loan principal of RMB 39.95 million and the corresponding interest (interest as of November 20, 2006 is RMB 7,067,934.41; from November 21, 2006 until full repayment, interest shall be paid at the overdue loan interest rate stipulated in the Loan Contract (430108001) Nongyin Jie Zi (2003) No. 0062 dated December 31, 2003). The above payment obligation shall be fulfilled within 10 days after this judgment takes legal effect. If not fulfilled within the time limit, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. 2. If Jinfan Company fails to perform the above debt, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch shall have the right to priority repayment from the proceeds of the land use rights of the planned plots No. 5 and No. 7 in Jinxia New District, Kaifu District, Changsha City (land parcel numbers both 5999997, mortgage area for Plot No. 5 is 48,563.34 square meters, mortgage area for Plot No. 7 is 55,585.48 square meters) provided by Jinxia Company as collateral. 3. After Jinxia Company bears the above mortgage guarantee liability, it has the right to seek recourse from Jinfan Company. The case acceptance fee of RMB 242,116 shall be borne by Jinfan Company.

Jinxia Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, stating: 1. ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company intentionally concealed the important fact of "new loan to repay old loan" in the loan contract provided to Jinxia Company. Jinxia Company's contract differs from the contract held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch in several respects. Jinfan Company added the words "new loan to repay old loan" to the original document it held and placed it in the archives of the Land and Resources Bureau to assist ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch in asserting its rights against Jinxia Company. ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company engaged in malicious collusion to defraud Jinxia Company into providing the guarantee. According to the Guarantee Law, Jinxia Company should not bear mortgage guarantee liability. 2. Jinxia Company should not bear mortgage guarantee liability because it was unaware that the loan of December 31, 2003 was a "new loan to repay old loan." 3. The loan of December 31, 2002, since it was not consented to in writing by Jinxia Company and had no mortgage limit, should be deemed as not having been provided with a mortgage guarantee by Jinxia Company. Jinxia Company did not provide a mortgage guarantee for the loan of December 31, 2002, so this case does not constitute a continuation relationship between the new loan and the old loan. The court of first instance erred in ordering the appellant to bear mortgage guarantee liability on the grounds that the new loan and the old loan were guaranteed by the same guarantor. 4. The calculation of interest in this case is erroneous. Jinxia Company requests the second instance court to: 1. revoke items 2 and 3 of the judgment of the court of first instance according to law, and reject ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch's claims against Jinxia Company; 2. order ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

In response to Jinxia Company's appeal claims and reasons, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch argued: 1. Jinxia Company knew that the purpose of Jinfan Company's loan of December 31, 2003 was "new loan to repay old loan." First, in the original Loan Contract submitted by Jinxia Company to the Changsha Land and Resources Bureau, the "Loan Purpose" column clearly stated: "working capital for new loan to repay old loan." Second, when the loan originally guaranteed by Jinfan Company was not informed to be repaid, and Jinfan Company requested a mortgage guarantee for a loan of the same amount from Jinxia Company, requiring the same collateral, as the same guarantor for both the new and old loans of Jinfan Company, Jinxia Company could not have been completely ignorant of the purpose of this loan. Third, even according to the Loan Contract submitted by Jinxia Company itself in the first instance, Jinfan Company's use of the loan for "new loan to repay old loan" did not exceed the scope of working capital use and did not violate the Loan Contract's provisions. 2. Jinxia Company is the same guarantor for the three loans of Jinfan Company in 2001, 2002, and 2003, both new and old. 3. The parties' stipulations in this case regarding loan interest rates and overdue loan interest rates comply with laws and administrative regulations, do not violate relevant regulations or industry policies, and should be protected by law. In conclusion, Jinxia Company is both the same guarantor for Jinfan Company's new and old loans and knows the purpose of the guaranteed loan, so it should bear guarantee liability. ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch requests the second instance court to dismiss Jinxia Company's claims according to law.

In response to Jinxia Company's appeal claims and reasons, Jinfan Company argued: From the signing of the Loan Contract (430108001) Nongyin Jie Zi (2001) No. 041 on December 29, 2001, to the signing of the Loan Contract (430108001) Nongyin Jie Zi (2002) No. 047 on December 31, 2002, and the signing of the Loan Contract (430108001) Nongyin Jie Zi (2003) No. 062 on December 31, 2003, all were the same loan being rolled over with a new loan to repay the old loan, and this loan was always guaranteed by Jinxia Company with the land parcels No. 5 and No. 7 in Jinxia New District as collateral, with no change in the form of guarantee from beginning to end. Therefore, Jinxia Company's assertion in its grounds of appeal that Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch engaged in malicious collusion to harm the legitimate rights and interests of Jinxia Company is contrary to objective facts. Under the condition that the parties to the contract—the lender, borrower, mortgagor, and collateral—remained unchanged and the debt was not repaid, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch would not harm its own interests to fulfill the borrower's demands, nor would it agree to Jinxia Company providing the already pledged collateral as a guarantee for another loan. After ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch issued the "Reply to Changsha Jinxia Development and Construction Co., Ltd.'s Letter to Our Bank Dated December 31, 2002" to Jinxia Company, Jinxia Company did not raise any further objections, indicating that Jinxia Company had affirmed the objective fact of the "new loan to repay old loan" from the beginning. Even if it were established that Jinxia Company only learned of the "new loan to repay old loan" nature of the 2003 Loan Contract through a material misunderstanding on December 31, 2004, pursuant to Article 55 of the Contract Law, Jinxia Company has lost its right to rescind. In conclusion, Jinxia Company's grounds of appeal that Jinfan Company and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch engaged in malicious collusion to harm the legitimate rights and interests of Jinxia Company have no factual basis. Jinfan Company requests the second instance court to render a fair judgment according to law.

Upon second instance trial, this Court affirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

This Court additionally finds that on December 31, 2003, the Changsha Land and Resources Bureau issued a Business Acceptance Receipt numbered 20031231004 to Jinxia Company, stating: Your unit's comrade Ding Li applied for record-filing of state-owned land use rights mortgage (including renewal and modification) on December 31, 2003. Our bureau has accepted the application. Please send personnel to arrange related matters within 7 working days.

This Court opines that the Loan Contract (430108001) Nongyin Jie Zi (2003) No. 0062 signed between ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company represents the true intentions of the parties, does not violate prohibitive provisions of law, and is valid according to law. Jinfan Company, having failed to repay the corresponding loan after the contract's maturity, should perform the civil liability of repaying the loan principal and interest. The debtor, Jinfan Company, did not object to the relevant content of the court of first instance's judgment requiring it to perform its debt, and this Court affirms this.

To ensure the performance of the above loan contract, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinxia Company signed two Mortgage Contracts, (430108001) Nongyin Di Zi (2003) No. 0053 and (430108001) Nongyin Di Zi (2003) No. 0054, and completed the relevant mortgage registration procedures. The above mortgage contracts represent the true intentions of the parties, do not violate prohibitive provisions of law, and are valid according to law. If Jinfan Company fails to perform the related debt, Jinxia Company should fulfill its guarantee obligations in accordance with the mortgage contracts.

Jinxia Company, on the grounds that the content of the loan contract it holds differs from the loan contract provided by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, claims that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company engaged in malicious collusion, intentionally concealed the important content of "new loan to repay old loan," and defrauded Jinxia Company into providing the guarantee. However, discrepancies in the content of contracts held by different parties can result from various complex objective reasons, and cannot simply be determined as intentional fraud by one party to the contract. If Jinxia Company claims that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company engaged in malicious collusion and fraud, it should provide other evidence to prove it. Jinxia Company asserts that Jinfan Company added the words "new loan to repay old loan" to the original contract when handling the mortgage registration procedures to assist ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch in asserting rights against Jinxia Company. As a matter of common sense, the party applying for mortgage registration procedures should be the mortgagor, not the creditor; based on the evidence in this case, the Business Acceptance Receipt provided by the Changsha Land and Resources Bureau clearly records that the person handling the mortgage registration procedures in this case was Jinxia Company's agent, "Ding Li." Jinxia Company, as the principal, should bear civil liability for the agent's acts. Jinxia Company did not provide corresponding evidence to prove that the creditor, ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch, participated in the mortgage registration procedures, and its appeal claim that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch committed intentional fraud cannot be established.

According to Article 54, Paragraph 2 and Article 55 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where a contract is concluded through fraud, duress, or exploitation of a party's difficulties, causing the other party to act contrary to its true intentions, the injured party has the right to request a People's Court or an arbitration institution to modify or rescind the contract. The right to rescind is extinguished if the party entitled to rescind does not exercise it within one year from the date it knew or should have known of the grounds for rescission. In a letter dated December 31, 2004, Jinxia Company stated to ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch that it had learned that the purpose of Jinfan Company's loan was to repay old loans with new loans. If Jinxia Company believed that ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch and Jinfan Company had engaged in fraud when concluding the contract, it should have applied to a People's Court or arbitration institution to modify or rescind the contract no later than December 31, 2005. Since Jinxia Company did not exercise its right to rescind within that period, even if the mortgage contract contained grounds for rescission, its right to rescind has been extinguished. Jinxia Company's refusal to perform its contractual obligations in this case on the grounds of fraud by the contracting parties is inconsistent with legal provisions, and this Court does not support it.

Although there are some discrepancies in the content of the loan contracts held by the parties in this case, the parties do not dispute the authenticity of the contracts they respectively hold, which does not preclude the determination of the contract's formation. Jinxia Company's main reason for claiming exemption from its guarantee obligation is that the loan purpose in the loan contract it holds is "working capital" loan, which differs from the loan purpose of "working capital loan for new loan to repay old loan" in the loan contract held by ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch. Enterprise working capital, as opposed to fixed assets, refers to an enterprise's cash assets, including funds used for paying wages, purchasing raw materials, repaying debts, etc. Jinxia Company agreed to provide a guarantee for Jinfan Company's "working capital" loan. Jinfan Company's use of the loan to repay matured debts did not exceed the scope of Jinxia Company's guarantee. Before the signing of the contracts in this case, Jinxia Company, Jinfan Company, and ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch had previously signed other loan mortgage contracts. Jinxia Company knew or should have known whether Jinfan Company had any outstanding debts at ABC Xianfeng Sub-branch. If Jinxia Company was unwilling to provide a mortgage for Jinfan Company's loan used to repay debts, it should have expressly restricted it in the contract. In this case, Jinxia Company made a broad commitment to provide a guarantee for Jinfan Company's "working capital" loan without restricting the loan purpose. Now, in litigation, its objection to the borrower using the loan to repay debts violates the principle of good faith.

Article 39 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where the parties to the principal contract agree to use a new loan to repay an old loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known of such agreement. Where the new loan and the old loan are guaranteed by the same guarantor, the preceding paragraph shall not apply. In this case, Jinxia Company provided mortgage guarantees for both the new and old loans of Jinfan Company using the same collateral. Jinfan Company's use of the new loan to repay the old loan did not increase Jinxia Company's guarantee liability. Jinxia Company's appeal claim that its guarantee liability should be exempted is inconsistent with the above provision. Jinxia Company's appeal claim that the calculation of interest in this case is erroneous also lacks corresponding factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

In conclusion, the judgment of the court of first instance has clear findings of fact and correct application of law. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 242,116 shall be borne by Changsha Jinxia Development and Construction Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
